statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits at 11 of 100 in the low band, fourteen points below the 25 block threshold, while stress remains extreme at 85 and confidence is high at 89.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window covers the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH without reaching the block threshold.
headline: The overnight band stops widening: NQ holds 29,127.25 inside an unchanged 29,062.50 to 29,171.50 range, easing tail to 11, while a 4.944% ten-year, VIX 17.84 and crude above $100 keep stress extreme at 85 into the August consumer price report.
body:
The strongest new evidence this hour is an absence: the overnight range has stopped expanding. NQ trades 29,127.25, down 8.00 points or 0.03% against the 29,135.25 reference, inside a band of 29,062.50 to 29,171.50 that is identical to the band published an hour ago. Roughly four and a half hours have passed since the 22:00 UTC reopen and neither extreme has been extended. Price has instead worked back through the middle of the 109-point band, about 0.37% wide. A range that holds while price oscillates within it is the observable signature of working mean reversion, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path that tail risk measures. Tail therefore eases one point to 11 and the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON. A second independent quote source confirms the same level and the same band, so the reading does not rest on a single feed.

The backdrop remains genuinely difficult, which is why stress stays extreme at 85. The ten-year Treasury yield stands at 4.944%, up 10.7 basis points on the session and its highest since 2023, with an intraday high of 4.952% and the two-year reported near 4.53%. That bear-steepening tightens financial conditions directly on long-duration technology valuations. VIX closed at 17.84, up 8.38%, elevated in change terms though still moderate in absolute level. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,103.51, down 1.08%, and the major U.S. averages fell for a fourth consecutive session on 10 September. Cross-asset context collected overnight shows semiconductors as the weakest complex, down roughly three percent on average with six of seven names lower, while megacap performance was mixed. Futures-based context taken at the same time showed index futures marginally positive and volatility futures marginally lower, so nothing in the overnight cross-asset picture forms the aligned one-way amplifier stack that a higher tail reading would require.

Energy and geopolitics are the persistent stress engine rather than a current tail amplifier. WTI trades 102.88, up 0.39%, against a session high of 104.46, and Brent settled at 107.63 after climbing 6.3% to its highest level since May. The supply story behind those prices escalated materially on 10 September, when the tanker exchange in and around the Strait of Hormuz broadened into the largest declared wave of attacks on merchant shipping since the conflict began, following U.S. strikes on Iranian tankers on 5 and 8 September and Iranian missile fire near U.S. warships. Reporting counts at least 75 vessels attacked since the conflict opened, with a substantial queue of laden tankers waiting to transit. That is a structural condition that keeps stress extreme and leaves open-ended headline risk across the weekend closure, but it has not so far produced persistent directional structure in the index itself.

The August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC is the session's dominant checkpoint, confirmed on the official release schedule for 08:30 Eastern. Consensus sits near 0.4% monthly and 3.4% annual on headline, with core near 0.2% monthly and 2.4% annual and an unusually narrow forecast range. Preliminary Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations follow at 14:00 UTC and the monthly budget statement at 18:00 UTC. Market pricing has carried meaningful odds of a Federal Reserve increase at the 15-16 September meeting, an unusual configuration that raises the sensitivity of the last inflation print before that decision. Ahead of a release, hypothetical post-event alignment is not treated as observed structure. The conditional path therefore peaks at tail 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot, inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold, easing to 21 across the cash open and 20 through the Michigan release before decaying back into the low band on the assumption that price discovery becomes orderly. The named invalidation is explicit: shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements would break that decay assumption. From 21:00 UTC the CME weekend closure removes the tradable path entirely and the conditional scores fall to a residual weekend-gap floor.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 02:00 UTC on 10 September to 01:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 11 and holds a tight 9 to 11 band through the U.S. overnight, the Asian session and the European morning, with the dominant mode recorded as mixed throughout. The regime change sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and the window peak of 24 at 13:00 UTC across the cash open, the only slot at the top of the watch band. It never crossed the 25 block threshold. From 14:00 UTC the series decays back into the low band at 17 and holds a 14 to 19 range through the U.S. afternoon and the close, with event/whipsaw recorded again at 19:00 and 20:00 UTC around the cash close and the maintenance halt. The final four hours settle at 15, 14, 13 and 12 as post-reopen trade proved contained. Stress never left the extreme band, rising from 81 to a peak of 87 and easing only to 85 at the end, which is the clearest signal in the series: a difficult, high-volatility environment persisted for a full 24 hours without the price path ever becoming pathological.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with roughly four and a half hours of observed post-reopen trade on 11 September and ends inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC the same day. Conditional tail starts at 11, holds 11 through the late Asian hours and settles at a 10 floor across the thinnest pre-European hours, where no U.S. macro is scheduled. From the European cash open it rebuilds gradually, 12 through 13, reaching 15 in the final full hour before the release as quoted depth thins. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report, which stays inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold because an inflation surprise more reliably produces two-sided whipsaw than a sustained no-retracement path. It eases to 21 across the 13:30 UTC cash open and holds 20 through the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release, the credible second information wave, then decays to 18 and back into the low band on the assumption that retracements reappear. The U.S. afternoon runs 16 down to 14, ticks back to 15 for the power hour as weekend risk reduction lands ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting, and settles at 13 after the cash close. From 21:00 UTC the venue is shut and conditional tail drops to 9 and then a 7 weekend floor that represents gap risk at the Sunday reopen rather than any tradable intraday path. Stress stays extreme from 85 to a 92 peak at the release before stepping out of the extreme band only when the market closes. The decay after the release is an assumption, not an observation, and its named invalidation is shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements.
